title: XR panels not rendering after IWSDK 1.0.1 upgrade (branch feat/iwsdk-1.0.1)
description:
After upgrading IWSDK 0.3.1 to 1.0.1 (branch feat/iwsdk-1.0.1, uncommitted), none of the XR uikit panels are visible when entering XR in the IWER emulator. Controllers and the grab bar render. tsc and vite build pass, and all 7 ui/*.json compile identically.

Findings so far (via iwsdk-dev MCP):
- Console has no errors, only a THREE.WebGLProgram shader precision warning (likely unrelated).
- XR session is active (Meta Quest 3, emulated, immersive-ar).
- All 6 panel entities (indices 17 to 22) have PanelUI and PanelDocument, so the UI JSON loaded and parsed.
- Library panel (entity 20) is visible, has RayInteractable, local position (0, 0.2815, 0) under the grab bar, entity scale 1.
- Not yet read: the UIKitDocument group's own scale (child of the panel entity).

Context:
- 1.0.1 removed PanelUI maxWidth/maxHeight ("world-space size is controlled exclusively by the entity transform"). 0.3.1 re-applied document.setTargetDimensions(maxW/worldScale, maxH/worldScale) every frame.
- Workaround added in src/xr/PanelSizeSystem.ts: registerPanelSize(entity, w, h) plus a PanelSizeSystem that calls doc.setTargetDimensions once on the PanelDocument qualify event. It may run before the root element size is known, leaving the document at scale 0, NaN or tiny (UIKitDocument.updateScaling bails to scale 1 only when target <= 0).
- Sizes: 0.4x0.3 for settings, song, play, calibration and tuner. 1.0x0.525 for library.
- Also possible: a 1.0.1 render or parenting change unrelated to sizing, or not a regression at all (no A/B against 0.3.1 in the same emulator yet).
design: Next steps: (1) read the UIKitDocument group scale for entity 20 via scene_get_object_transform. (2) A/B with the registerPanelSize calls commented out to see natural-size rendering. (3) If scale is the cause, re-apply target dimensions every frame like 0.3.1 or apply once rootElement.size is known. Reference: IWSDK 1.0.1 dist/ui/document.js updateScaling, dist/ui/ui.js loadPanel.
acceptance_criteria: All XR panels render at the intended sizes (0.4x0.3, library 1.0x0.525) on entering XR in the IWER emulator, with no new console errors. Panel interaction (ray hover and click) still works.
notes: Package changes on the branch: @iwsdk/core 1.0.1, @iwsdk/vite-plugin-dev 1.0.1, @iwsdk/vite-plugin-uikitml 0.4.2, @types/three 0.181.0. The sharp override can likely be dropped after this lands (plugin-dev 1.0.1 needs sharp ^0.35.4). Do not merge to main until panels render.

description: When the desktop page is narrowed, or opened on a phone, clickable areas no longer line up with the drawn buttons. Which screens and by how much is not yet recorded. (2) canvas {100vw/100vh} and #screen-container {fixed; inset:0} in v2/desktop.html disagree on mobile where 100vh includes browser chrome, switch to dvh or inset-based sizing. title: Spike: compare Polyphon (PitchPlease) and Poly Peach for mic piano note detection
description: Evaluate open-source polyphonic note detectors for the mic-to-piano-keys feature. Polyphon: github.com/markusstrasser/pitchplease (npm @markusstrasser/pitchplease v3.1.0, MIT, TS types, AudioWorklet+WASM SIMD, models fast/piano/voice/fft). Poly Peach: npm poly-peach 0.5.1 (LGPL, gitlab.com/chrisspen/poly-peach, last published 2023-10, targeted detection of expected notes via WASM FFT). Basic Pitch is likely too heavy for live XR (CQT needs >1s chunks, ONNX runtime ~12MB), not benchmarked.
design: Polyphon is the stronger candidate (maintained, MIT, streaming 40-50ms latency, self-reported piano F1 0.68-0.73, 12-20% audio-thread load on M3 Pro). Poly Peach fits known-chart play but has LGPL and stale maintenance. Neither tested on Quest.
acceptance_criteria: Run Polyphon fast and piano on Quest Browser and record stats.cpuLoad and stats.kernel. Prototype Poly Peach against a known chart if LGPL is acceptable. Record accuracy, latency and CPU for both in a doc and recommend one.
notes:
Research done 2026-11-20 via npm registry and READMEs. Benchmarks are the authors' own and unverified. Basic Pitch heaviness is an inference, no browser or Quest numbers were found.
Quest runs 2026-11-21 (log 2026-11-21-mic-note-detection-spike). Polyphon piano: wasm-relaxed kernel, cpuLoad 0.68-0.72, ~86 fps, latency 27-37 ms. Output flickers in single-frame blips (median 7-9 ms). Played notes reach prob 0.9-1.0 sustained, 0.4-0.7 in decay. Phantoms below C3 (A#1-E2) mean prob 0.70, 19 of 204 at >=0.9, so one threshold cannot separate them. Poly Peach 0.5.1 has no WASM (bead was wrong), is a DOM-bound demo needing tone. Only Chromagram is reusable, C3-B6 only, ~0.7 s window, LGPL, 23 MB. Output is steadier (median 64 ms) but has ghost semitone clusters and harmonics at 50-60% of the loudest note. Leaning Polyphon plus an expected-notes filter. Not done: fast/voice runs, expected-notes filter, scored accuracy, LGPL decision, recommendation doc.

title: Wait mode: hold the song until the correct note is played
description: Why: a practice mode where the highway waits for the right note, as in Sightread and PianoBooster. It is the closest Play counterpart to the tuner, which holds until the note is right. Follow-up unlocked by keyboard MIDI input ([[keyboard-midi-input]]). Keys scoring must exist first. Link that bead as a dependency when it is filed.
design: Proposed, not final. Shared wait gate reads notesDetected and holds the clock at the next unhit note, so it does not need to know the instrument. Note matching stays per instrument. Chord rule: keys needs every note, guitar needs any one. Separate saved settings waitModeKeys and waitModeGuitar, both off by default. Guitar covers lead, rhythm and bass, and its toggle stays hidden until tested with real playing. Order: keys first, then try guitar on single-note parts. Guitar limits: NoteDetector takes one polled pitch, ignores octaves, and has no onset detection, so a ringing note could pass a repeated note. Needs a waiting state separate from user pause so the Play button stays correct. Open: should song audio stop while waiting (recommended) or keep going. SongPlayer.play() builds a new SoundTouch node each time, so test stop and restart for clicks or lag. Guitar in XR depends on RockyRoad-0q4.10 because XR Play has no note detection.
acceptance_criteria: With waitModeKeys on, the highway stops at the next unhit note and resumes when it is played. Seek, rollback and difficulty changes reset the gate cleanly. User pause and automatic waiting are distinguishable in the UI. Audio restart behavior is tested and acceptable.
notes: 2026-11-21 update: Keys scoring now exists. NoteScorer (src/shared/NoteScorer.ts) replaced NoteDetector (now tests/legacy) and notesDetected feeds both instruments. Polyphon scoring runs on desktop behind ?input=polyphon (epic RockyRoad-kvg). The wait gate can read notesDetected as designed. For the mic, chords are a known gap (lowest triad note about 40 percent in close low voicings), so keys wait mode should favor MIDI (RockyRoad-n6k.1). Depends on the UI wiring in RockyRoad-n6k.

title: XR: gate note scoring and re-tune on whether the user tuned (design, undecided)
description:
NO DECISION MADE. This records the 2026-10-18 discussion so it can be settled later.

Context: XR Play no longer auto-opens the tuner (only a USB mic works reliably, so tuning is optional via the Song page Tune button, see RockyRoad-0q4.5). XR Play also has no PitchDetector or NoteDetector, so it never says whether notes are right. Most XR users will not tune, so they should not get right/wrong feedback. Users who did tune could get it, and could be re-tuned automatically when they open a song with different tuningOffsets.

Idea under discussion:
- Scoring needs a working mic and the tuner is the only place XR confirms one, so "has tuned" is a proxy for "can be scored".
- Re-tune only matters when scoring is on. It would be a consequence (scoring on and the part's tuningOffsets differ from the last completed tuning, desktop's lastTuningKey rule) rather than its own setting.

Options considered:
- Two layers: derived capability (tuned this session, in memory, not shown) plus one persisted xrScoring preference (default off, in Settings). Tuning never changes the preference, so nothing flips a visible setting behind the user's back.
- One bool: completing the first tune turns xrScoring on once, then the user owns it (needs a hidden "seen" flag).
- Rejected as odd: auto-flipping a visible scoring toggle every time a tune completes.

Open questions:
- Is the toggle a Settings item or a Song page choice next to Tune?
- Is "tuned" session-only (matches desktop, but the Quest browser reloads often) or persisted?
- With scoring off, hide the right/wrong feedback UI entirely or just stop updating it?

Dependencies and caveats:
- Needs note detection in XR Play (NoteDetector plus a per-frame PitchDetector.detect(), as desktop ActiveSceneScreen does). That is not built and may be its own bead.
- The tuner's chosen input device is not persisted (XRTunerScene._inputId). Scoring in Play would fall back to the weak built-in mic, so the USB device must be remembered, with a fallback when its deviceId is gone.
- Once scoring exists, handing the tuner's live detector into Play avoids a second mic request.
- Guitar and bass only. Keys keep today's behavior.
